terms: Setting: one combination of backbone (CBraMod, REVE, DINOv3), dataset (BCI, MA, Speech), and depth (early, middle, late), giving 27 in total (Section 2, Backbones and data).
TopK SAE: c=ReLU(TopK_k((x−b_dec)W_enc+b_enc)), x̂=cW_dec+b_dec, with k=32, trained with MSE plus AuxK (Section 2, TopK SAEs).
Alpha vs sham test: an 8–12 Hz band-stop compared with a width-matched 30–34 Hz notch, both fourth-order zero-phase Butterworth filters (Section 2, Perturbations).
Response metrics: sparse-code cosine, active-set Jaccard, and per-latent |Δf_j| (Section 2, Perturbations).

Distortion control: the SAE response divided either by time-domain ‖x−x̃‖₂/‖x‖₂ or by the fraction of spectral energy removed. Removed-energy ratios are 57.2/34.6/11.8 on BCI/MA/Speech (Section 2, Perturbations).
Specialist-like alpha latent: in the top quartile of alpha selectivity and at or below median channel-dropout fragility (Section 2, Selectivity).

Controls: size-matched general-fragile and random groups for readout tests; activity-matched non-specialists (nearest in clean firing rate and mean activation) for clean-alpha tests (Section 2; Appendix A).

Importance: |w_j|·E_train[c_j] from logistic probes on mean-pooled codes. Group ablation zeroes a selected set of codes and measures the change in balanced accuracy, either with a frozen probe or a retrained one (Section 2).
Independent observational validation: correlation of a latent's clean activation with trial-wise relative alpha power, a quantity not used in selection (Section 2).

Validation ladder: Stages 1–3 test sensitivity, distortion-controlled selectivity, and specificity. Stage 5 (observational validation) completes the representational claim. Stage 4 (readout intervention) is required only for a task-relevance claim (Section 1, Table 1, Figure 1).
Bootstrap CIs: 10,000 resamples over settings, not over latents (Section 2).
